mentions.name: Snapalabra
mentions.description: A visual language learning app where users look at an image and describe what they see in their target language. The app gives LLM feedback on what the user writes and provides clues mapped to each image. It is a free supplementary tool for short daily sessions (like a 5-minute coffee-break activity), not a full language course, and is currently used for intermediate Spanish and beginner Irish.
mentions.problem: The author could understand a lot of spoken Spanish but struggled to construct sentences on the fly when speaking; a few minutes of daily active practice helps build sentence construction and exposes gaps in understanding.
mentions.audience: Language learners already taking classes and consuming content in their target language who want a short, supplementary daily practice activity
mentions.source_excerpt:
Working on a visual language learning app called Snapalabra!

The idea is simple: You look at an image and describe what you see in your target language. That's basically it!
